recent_commits.message: docs(normalize): close the header-zone DOI residual by measurement, not by hunch
recent_commits.body:
The one identifier H0 still drops that it should not
(10.24072/pci.rr.101017.rev11, a bioRxiv preprint URL) was recorded as a known
residual with a rationale and no number. A rationale is not a measurement, so
the obvious widening was measured before being rejected rather than argued
about -- two-sided, over the same 297 English papers, counting what it would
save AND what it would cost.

Widening the exemption from "previous line ends in a colon" to "previous line
does not end in sentence-terminal punctuation" would:

    recover  0 real identifiers
    stop   198 correct masthead-furniture drops

It is not a weaker colon rule, it is the wrong signal. The residual's own
lead-in ends in a period, so it sits on the same side of that line as the
masthead cases and no punctuation signal separates it.

Comment only: no non-comment line changes, output is byte-identical, so
NORMALIZATION_VERSION and __version__ are deliberately unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): the region was sized to the caption, so published columns and rows were deleted
recent_commits.body:
Four defects in table-region detection, each deleting real printed data from the
structured table with no error, no warning and no log line.

10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.39337 Table 3 prints seven columns; docpluck
emitted two. Five of six data columns -- and the Sodium and Physical-activity
values of the surviving one -- appeared ZERO times in the 59 KB render.

(a) _horizontal_rules_in required a ruled line to be entirely CONTAINED in the
    search band, which is built at the CAPTION's x-range. On p9 the caption
    spans 141pt and each of Table 3's twenty rules spans 515pt, so all twenty
    were rejected while ten 10pt row decorations were kept -- still enough to
    clear LATTICE_MIN_HORIZONTAL_RULES, so lattice fired on furniture. Now
    keyed on x-OVERLAP, safe for a rule because a rule does not cross a column
    gutter.
(b) A rule drawn cell-by-cell arrives as one segment per column, so it only
    overlaps the band where the caption sits (ieee_access_2 p55: one segment of
    a three-column grid). Collinear end-to-end segments are merged first.
(c) _longest_aligned_run compared column START edges only, so a run severed
    where a right-aligned cell changed width. 10.1371/journal.pmed.1004323 p10:
    `fenylefrine 0 3` and `ephedrine 0 2` begin ~29pt right of the rows above
    but END on the same edge, and were cut off. A column now counts as aligned
    on its START or its END edge.
(d) A located region kept the MODAL body row's width, so a column filled only
    in the header and one summary row fell outside it -- Rel. risk
    1.19 (0.33-4.31) and P value 1.00. The region is widened to the rows it
    already contains that begin at its left edge; gated OFF for caption_only,
    where no grid was found and widening is the known cog_emo regression.

Table 4 of that paper also stops being a copy of Table 3, so the
surgical-reintervention rows reach a structured table for the first time.

Measured, two-sided and deterministically: over 40 PDFs sampled
random.Random(20260912) from a 10,049-PDF repository (25 with >=1 table
caption, 62 captioned regions) column-clipped regions fall 43 -> 34, 7 papers
improved, 0 worsened -- (a)+(b) only, since the clip detector shares (d)'s
criterion and cannot judge it. On the 6-paper canary set 2 renders changed and
3 are byte-identical; a token census over both changed renders shows 0 tokens
lost and 0 vanished.

Ground truth is the rasterized page throughout, never another extractor.
Both test files were watched RED first. TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION 2.4.14 ->
2.4.15: consumers read it as the identity of the pipeline that made a table.

Also fixes the docs-consistency gate, which was red at c120788: __version__ and
NORMALIZATION_VERSION were bumped without updating docs/README.md.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): a DOI on its own continuation line is reference data
recent_commits.body:
Three rules deleted it. P0's two curated DOI-line patterns fired
document-wide on the strength of a comment claiming "in-text DOI mentions
... never appear alone" -- false, because a reference whose DOI wraps is
exactly that. H0 added a third route: its header zone is a flat 30-line
cap with no content end-condition, so on a short document it reaches the
bibliography and the generic bare-URL banner pattern matched a DOI on the
"doi.org" host.

The arithmetic, over 300 PDFs sampled random.Random(20260912) from a
10,049-PDF corpus (297 English; 1 spanish, 1 portuguese, 1 bilingual
excluded and reported): the two P0 patterns fired 649 times across 117 of
297 papers (39.4%) on a unique standalone DOI inside a References span --
every one a destroyed identifier -- and 27 times in 2 papers on a genuine
per-page journal footer. 27/676 = 4.0% accuracy, the same arithmetic that
condemned the EU-numeric rules and W0k.

Verified at the primary source: 10.1525/collabra.138502 prints 133 DOIs
and the academic render delivered 101, losing all 32 of its
standalone-DOI lines.

The genuine footer is not lost with them. A journal stamps its own DOI on
every page, so that line recurs; P0r already strips on >= 3 standalone
repetitions and _BARE_DOI_IDENTIFIER_LINE adds the shape there, verified
firing on real papers (19 -> 0 and 7 -> 0). The line content is identical
in both cases and can never separate them; recurrence can, and recurrence
is what a running footer is.

H0 gains two content end-conditions, each measured separately: no line
inside a _find_references_spans span is header furniture, and a
DOI-identifier line introduced by a colon-terminated lead-in is the object
of a sentence. The colon discriminator recovers 4 of 5 real identifiers
and costs 1 of 120 furniture drops.

Corpus re-measured after the fix: 649 reference-DOI losses -> 1. The
residual (10.24072/pci.rr.101017.rev11, a bioRxiv URL with no colon
lead-in) is recorded in the code rather than coded around -- one paper
proves a shape exists and says nothing about prevalence.

DOCX and HTML are unaffected; those branches never call normalize_text,
checked at the source and by probe.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.66 -> 1.9.67 even though the change mostly
removes rules: consumers store extracted text keyed on it, so leaving it
would make pre-fix and post-fix text indistinguishable in their store --
and the pre-fix text is missing published identifiers.

Pinned by tests/test_standalone_doi_line_is_reference_data.py, proved red
by re-inserting the deleted patterns at runtime and by neutralising the
references-span exemption. Carries three two-sided controls: an inline DOI
still survives, a recurring page footer is still stripped, and a genuine
publisher landing-page banner is still stripped.

Canary: the audit reported 5 findings on ip_feldman_2025_pspb. All 5 are
PRE-EXISTING and untouched by this change, proved against a clean HEAD
worktree render rather than asserted: the HEAD and post-fix renders are
3221 lines each and differ in exactly 6 lines, every one a reference
gaining its DOI, nothing removed. Each of the 5 flagged strings occurs the
same number of times in both renders. They are real defects in docpluck's
output and are reported separately rather than folded into this change.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0g comes out of both text channels — a CI does not tell you which statistic it belongs to
recent_commits.body:
`W0g_dropped_minus_ci_pairing` re-signed a bare positive decimal whenever a bracket in the
same record made the arithmetic work. IT NEVER CHECKED WHICH STATISTIC THE BRACKET
DESCRIBED. On `korbmacher_2022_kruger` the page prints, and pdftotext delivers verbatim:

    r(223) = -0.13 (p = .0498, 95% CI [-0.26, -0.0002])

The interval is `r`'s. W0g took the nearest bare positive decimal in the record — the
P-VALUE — and published `p = -.0498`. A probability cannot be negative. The same paper
yields `p = -.05` from the second occurrence of the shape.

AND IT WAS IN THE SHIPPED OUTPUT, not merely in a re-normalization. The handoff that
scoped this work recorded it as pass-2 only, which reads as an idempotency curiosity. The
render channel called W0g over markdown `normalize_text` had ALREADY normalized, so that
call was itself a second pass: `render_pdf_to_markdown` emitted both fabricated values on
the FIRST render. Raw pdftotext escapes only because it delivers the bracket with EN
DASHES, which W0g's pattern does not match; S5 makes them ASCII and the next pass fires.

THE WIDER COST, confirmed against the rasterized page: over 250 papers W0g fired 12 times
in 4, and at least 7 of those rewrote a quantity that is non-negative by definition —
`SE = 0.11` -> `SE = -0.11`, `p = .90` -> `p = -.90`. `10.1525/collabra.118835` p7 prints
`(hedges' g = -.17, SE = 0.11, 95%CI = [-0.38, 0.04], p = .12)`: a negative estimate with a
POSITIVE standard error, the paper's house style on that page. There was no corruption to
repair.

THE THREE TIERS directive names CI CONTAINMENT verbatim as forbidden evidence, and W0g is
CI containment by name. Its signature is `text: str`, so it can never consult the rendered
page. CHECK THE SIGNATURE BEFORE YOU CHECK THE LOGIC. A "skip the token after `p =`" guard
would fix one paper and not the class: the rule cannot tell which statistic an interval
describes, because that is a fact about the SENTENCE.

BOTH CHANNELS, and only two exist. Verified by grep rather than assumed from this repo's
usual three-channel phrasing: W0g was never wired into `tables/cell_cleaning.py`.

W0b, W0d, W0q, W0h AND W0m ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. A FAMILY VERDICT MUST BE TESTED PER
MEMBER. CLAUDE.md twice records "W0b/W0d/W0g fire 0 times in 226 papers" and that line is
WRONG for the first two — they fire on `efendic_2022_affect` and recover 62 real minus
signs correctly, `r = 2.74 [20.92, 20.30]` back to `r = -.74 [-0.92, -0.30]`. Sweeping the
family out together would have destroyed published values. A control test pins them.

G5c2 IS NOW IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION, and that was the whole of the remaining corpus
gate. `_rejoin_split_numbered_headings` emits `N. <Heading>`, and its own output was
eligible as its own INPUT: the stacked-orphan guard only saw a BARE `^N.$`, and
`lookup_canonical_label` strips one leading number, so `6. References` still qualified as a
target and a stray `3.` above it was glued on. `3. 6. References` resolves to None, so the
partitioner LOSES the heading. All four remaining non-idempotent papers were this one
shape — efendic_2022_affect, am_sociol_rev_4, nat_comms_3, bmc_med_4 — with DIGIT COUNTS
IDENTICAL across all four, which is why no digit-delta check could ever have found it.

THE RATCHET WAS NOT RAISED. It stays at 0 and the corpus gate now passes on its own terms:
5 non-idempotent papers -> 0, by fixing the causes. The owner was offered a named-defect
list and a raise to 4 and chose to fix the cause before releasing.

`NORMALIZATION_VERSION` 1.9.65 -> 1.9.66. It MUST bump even though this only REMOVES a
rewrite: consumers store extracted text keyed on that string, so leaving it would make text
produced before and after indistinguishable in their store. `TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION`
stays at 2.4.14 — no table code changed.

Two test files, both watched RED first (8 failures on G5c2, 2 on W0g, controls passing) and
both asserting through `normalize_text` / `render_pdf_to_markdown`, never the raw function:
a test that calls a deliberately-kept definition keeps failing after its call sites are
gone, because it measures the definition rather than the product. That trap cost a cycle on
the W0k removal.

Two instrument defects were found and fixed while writing them, both recorded in the files
because both are this repo's own recurring traps: the stacked-heading detector first used
`\s+`, which matches a NEWLINE, so it spanned the three CORRECT lines and reported a defect
on a repaired paper; and it ended in `\S`, which matched a run of bare list numbers. A
render-chain gate that asserted a magic `len(names) >= 50` now asserts that two independent
derivations of the chain AGREE, because a fixed floor can only ever be too low to catch a
blinding or tripped by a deliberate retirement — and it was the second.

Three stale imports of the already-retired W0k/W0l rules are dropped from render.py. They
had sat unused since f169c3d; an unused import of a retired rule reads as though the rule
were still in the pipeline.

Verified: full suite 3209 passed / 0 failed; render_deletion_scan 26/26 papers 0 content
lost; repair_site_scan 120/120; article custody 0 leaks in all three forms; a three-provider
consult round (anthropic/openai/xai, 3 answered 0 refused, all passing the read-the-code
challenge) returned 0 findings. The one adjacent case it raised — a DOTLESS numbering
convention can still stack — was measured at 0 occurrences in 101 papers against a
two-sided control and deliberately left unfixed rather than widened on a constructed string.

recent_commits.message: Fix .batch_query() crashing on a connection-level failure
recent_commits.body:
req_error(is_error = \(resp) FALSE) only suppresses errors on a real
HTTP status; a connection-level failure (timeout, DNS, dropped
connection) still comes back from req_perform_sequential's
on_error = "continue" as an httr2_failure condition object, not a
response. Every archive-*.R caller checks only is.null(resp) before
calling httr2::resp_status(resp), which crashes on that object
instead. Normalizes any non-response result to NULL in the one
shared helper instead of patching every caller individually.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0g comes out of both text channels — a CI does not tell you which statistic it belongs to
recent_commits.body:
`W0g_dropped_minus_ci_pairing` re-signed a bare positive decimal whenever a bracket in the
same record made the arithmetic work. IT NEVER CHECKED WHICH STATISTIC THE BRACKET
DESCRIBED. On `korbmacher_2022_kruger` the page prints, and pdftotext delivers verbatim:

    r(223) = -0.13 (p = .0498, 95% CI [-0.26, -0.0002])

The interval is `r`'s. W0g took the nearest bare positive decimal in the record — the
P-VALUE — and published `p = -.0498`. A probability cannot be negative. The same paper
yields `p = -.05` from the second occurrence of the shape.

AND IT WAS IN THE SHIPPED OUTPUT, not merely in a re-normalization. The handoff that
scoped this work recorded it as pass-2 only, which reads as an idempotency curiosity. The
render channel called W0g over markdown `normalize_text` had ALREADY normalized, so that
call was itself a second pass: `render_pdf_to_markdown` emitted both fabricated values on
the FIRST render. Raw pdftotext escapes only because it delivers the bracket with EN
DASHES, which W0g's pattern does not match; S5 makes them ASCII and the next pass fires.

THE WIDER COST, confirmed against the rasterized page: over 250 papers W0g fired 12 times
in 4, and at least 7 of those rewrote a quantity that is non-negative by definition —
`SE = 0.11` -> `SE = -0.11`, `p = .90` -> `p = -.90`. `10.1525/collabra.118835` p7 prints
`(hedges' g = -.17, SE = 0.11, 95%CI = [-0.38, 0.04], p = .12)`: a negative estimate with a
POSITIVE standard error, the paper's house style on that page. There was no corruption to
repair.

THE THREE TIERS directive names CI CONTAINMENT verbatim as forbidden evidence, and W0g is
CI containment by name. Its signature is `text: str`, so it can never consult the rendered
page. CHECK THE SIGNATURE BEFORE YOU CHECK THE LOGIC. A "skip the token after `p =`" guard
would fix one paper and not the class: the rule cannot tell which statistic an interval
describes, because that is a fact about the SENTENCE.

BOTH CHANNELS, and only two exist. Verified by grep rather than assumed from this repo's
usual three-channel phrasing: W0g was never wired into `tables/cell_cleaning.py`.

W0b, W0d, W0q, W0h AND W0m ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. A FAMILY VERDICT MUST BE TESTED PER
MEMBER. CLAUDE.md twice records "W0b/W0d/W0g fire 0 times in 226 papers" and that line is
WRONG for the first two — they fire on `efendic_2022_affect` and recover 62 real minus
signs correctly, `r = 2.74 [20.92, 20.30]` back to `r = -.74 [-0.92, -0.30]`. Sweeping the
family out together would have destroyed published values. A control test pins them.

G5c2 IS NOW IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION, and that was the whole of the remaining corpus
gate. `_rejoin_split_numbered_headings` emits `N. <Heading>`, and its own output was
eligible as its own INPUT: the stacked-orphan guard only saw a BARE `^N.$`, and
`lookup_canonical_label` strips one leading number, so `6. References` still qualified as a
target and a stray `3.` above it was glued on. `3. 6. References` resolves to None, so the
partitioner LOSES the heading. All four remaining non-idempotent papers were this one
shape — efendic_2022_affect, am_sociol_rev_4, nat_comms_3, bmc_med_4 — with DIGIT COUNTS
IDENTICAL across all four, which is why no digit-delta check could ever have found it.

THE RATCHET WAS NOT RAISED. It stays at 0 and the corpus gate now passes on its own terms:
5 non-idempotent papers -> 0, by fixing the causes. The owner was offered a named-defect
list and a raise to 4 and chose to fix the cause before releasing.

`NORMALIZATION_VERSION` 1.9.65 -> 1.9.66. It MUST bump even though this only REMOVES a
rewrite: consumers store extracted text keyed on that string, so leaving it would make text
produced before and after indistinguishable in their store. `TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION`
stays at 2.4.14 — no table code changed.

Two test files, both watched RED first (8 failures on G5c2, 2 on W0g, controls passing) and
both asserting through `normalize_text` / `render_pdf_to_markdown`, never the raw function:
a test that calls a deliberately-kept definition keeps failing after its call sites are
gone, because it measures the definition rather than the product. That trap cost a cycle on
the W0k removal.

Two instrument defects were found and fixed while writing them, both recorded in the files
because both are this repo's own recurring traps: the stacked-heading detector first used
`\s+`, which matches a NEWLINE, so it spanned the three CORRECT lines and reported a defect
on a repaired paper; and it ended in `\S`, which matched a run of bare list numbers. A
render-chain gate that asserted a magic `len(names) >= 50` now asserts that two independent
derivations of the chain AGREE, because a fixed floor can only ever be too low to catch a
blinding or tripped by a deliberate retirement — and it was the second.

Three stale imports of the already-retired W0k/W0l rules are dropped from render.py. They
had sat unused since f169c3d; an unused import of a retired rule reads as though the rule
were still in the pipeline.

Verified: full suite 3209 passed / 0 failed; render_deletion_scan 26/26 papers 0 content
lost; repair_site_scan 120/120; article custody 0 leaks in all three forms; a three-provider
consult round (anthropic/openai/xai, 3 answered 0 refused, all passing the read-the-code
challenge) returned 0 findings. The one adjacent case it raised — a DOTLESS numbering
convention can still stack — was measured at 0 occurrences in 101 papers against a
two-sided control and deliberately left unfixed rather than widened on a constructed string.

recent_commits.message: Fix R-package-source-tree exclusion to only strip vendored dependencies
recent_commits.body:
A root-level DESCRIPTION+NAMESPACE package was always excluded outright,
which was correct for a vendored dependency but wrong whenever the
package itself IS the study's shared data/code deposit (e.g. a GitHub
repo like wx-ecology/BaBA, or a CRAN-published analysis package like
RRPP): the exclusion silently swept away the paper's own R/ source and
data/ files, with nothing surviving to recover them from. Now a
root-level package is only excluded when something other than standard
packaging scaffolding survives outside it (checked via
data_classify_files(), the same rules-based classifier data_check
itself uses, so "real content" means the same thing everywhere) --
otherwise the package IS the deposit and none of its files are
excluded. A package detected in a nested subfolder is still always
excluded, since a genuinely vendored copy (e.g. MGDrivE/ bundled
alongside a study's own Examples/) always has real content elsewhere in
the repo by construction.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Make skip_on_api_limit reach zip_peek() and every *_info() listing call via a session option
recent_commits.body:
Follow-up to 7573b210: that commit made skip_on_api_limit reach the
download-level path (download_repo_files() via data_check/code_check/
psychds_check), but two more call sites still had no way to receive it at
all, and both hit a real multi-hour Dryad quota-exhausted 429 wait live
during a full corpus rerun even with skip_on_api_limit = TRUE requested
throughout the reproducibility_check -> data_check chain:

1. repo_check()'s zip_peek() (reads a zip archive's file listing over HTTP
   Range requests, without downloading it) calls the SAME shared retry
   helpers download_repo_files() uses -- .storage_retry_after_factory(),
   .storage_is_transient_factory(), .wait_out_known_rate_limit() -- but has
   no skip_on_api_limit parameter of its own, and repo_check() has no way to
   pass one to it either. These three helpers now fall back to
   getOption("metacheck.skip_on_api_limit", FALSE) whenever their own
   argument is FALSE, so any caller that cannot thread the parameter through
   still gets the right behaviour.

2. Every *_info()/*_links() listing call across archive-*.R (Dryad, Zenodo,
   OSF, Dataverse, Figshare, Mendeley, DataONE, ReShare) shares ONE retry
   function, .batch_query() (R/utils.R), which hardcoded 429 as always
   retryable with no skip option at all -- completely separate from
   download_repo_files()'s retry machinery. It now also checks
   getOption("metacheck.skip_on_api_limit", FALSE) and treats a 429 as
   non-transient when set.

reproducibility_check() sets this option once, for its whole per-paper run
(same temporary-override pattern already used there for llm_use(), restored
unconditionally on exit), so every nested listing call -- however deep, and
regardless of whether that specific function's signature was ever updated
to accept skip_on_api_limit -- respects it without a parameter having to
fan out across ~10 archive backend files individually.
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix definer_lookup crash and thread cache/skip_on_api_limit through reproducibility_check's internal module calls
recent_commits.body:
1. reproducibility_check.R: definer_lookup <- character(0) is read later
   via definer_lookup[[key]] %||% "". `[[` on a named vector throws
   "subscript out of bounds" for a missing key instead of returning NULL,
   crashing on any symbol with 0 or >1 definers. Changed to list().
   Closes #402.

2. code_check.R / data_check.R: neither forwarded its own `cache` argument
   to the module_run(paper, "repo_check", ...) call it makes internally for
   the file listing, so repo_check() fell back to its own default
   (cache = FALSE) regardless of what the caller asked for -- every repo
   listing (Dryad/Zenodo/OSF/...) was re-queried from the host's API from
   scratch on every call. Fixed by forwarding cache = cache at both call
   sites in each file.

3. psychds_check.R / reproducibility_check.R: psychds_check()'s own
   fallback re-fetches data_check's file listing whenever
   get_prev_outputs("data_check", ...) is NULL -- which it always is when
   each module is invoked as a standalone module_run() call rather than a
   chained pipeline, exactly how reproducibility_check() calls it. But
   psychds_check() had no cache/skip_on_api_limit parameters at all, so
   this fallback always ran uncached and un-skip-aware, and
   reproducibility_check()'s own dispatcher excluded psychds_check from
   receiving either (on the assumption that only data_check/code_check
   download files). Net effect, confirmed live: even with
   cache = TRUE, skip_on_api_limit = TRUE requested end-to-end, this one
   fallback call silently ignored both and blocked for hours waiting out
   Dryad's daily quota reset instead of skipping. Fixed by adding both
   parameters to psychds_check() and forwarding them into its fallback
   call, and by including psychds_check in reproducibility_check()'s own
   forwarding list.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0g comes out of both text channels — a CI does not tell you which statistic it belongs to
recent_commits.body:
`W0g_dropped_minus_ci_pairing` re-signed a bare positive decimal whenever a bracket in the
same record made the arithmetic work. IT NEVER CHECKED WHICH STATISTIC THE BRACKET
DESCRIBED. On `korbmacher_2022_kruger` the page prints, and pdftotext delivers verbatim:

    r(223) = -0.13 (p = .0498, 95% CI [-0.26, -0.0002])

The interval is `r`'s. W0g took the nearest bare positive decimal in the record — the
P-VALUE — and published `p = -.0498`. A probability cannot be negative. The same paper
yields `p = -.05` from the second occurrence of the shape.

AND IT WAS IN THE SHIPPED OUTPUT, not merely in a re-normalization. The handoff that
scoped this work recorded it as pass-2 only, which reads as an idempotency curiosity. The
render channel called W0g over markdown `normalize_text` had ALREADY normalized, so that
call was itself a second pass: `render_pdf_to_markdown` emitted both fabricated values on
the FIRST render. Raw pdftotext escapes only because it delivers the bracket with EN
DASHES, which W0g's pattern does not match; S5 makes them ASCII and the next pass fires.

THE WIDER COST, confirmed against the rasterized page: over 250 papers W0g fired 12 times
in 4, and at least 7 of those rewrote a quantity that is non-negative by definition —
`SE = 0.11` -> `SE = -0.11`, `p = .90` -> `p = -.90`. `10.1525/collabra.118835` p7 prints
`(hedges' g = -.17, SE = 0.11, 95%CI = [-0.38, 0.04], p = .12)`: a negative estimate with a
POSITIVE standard error, the paper's house style on that page. There was no corruption to
repair.

THE THREE TIERS directive names CI CONTAINMENT verbatim as forbidden evidence, and W0g is
CI containment by name. Its signature is `text: str`, so it can never consult the rendered
page. CHECK THE SIGNATURE BEFORE YOU CHECK THE LOGIC. A "skip the token after `p =`" guard
would fix one paper and not the class: the rule cannot tell which statistic an interval
describes, because that is a fact about the SENTENCE.

BOTH CHANNELS, and only two exist. Verified by grep rather than assumed from this repo's
usual three-channel phrasing: W0g was never wired into `tables/cell_cleaning.py`.

W0b, W0d, W0q, W0h AND W0m ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. A FAMILY VERDICT MUST BE TESTED PER
MEMBER. CLAUDE.md twice records "W0b/W0d/W0g fire 0 times in 226 papers" and that line is
WRONG for the first two — they fire on `efendic_2022_affect` and recover 62 real minus
signs correctly, `r = 2.74 [20.92, 20.30]` back to `r = -.74 [-0.92, -0.30]`. Sweeping the
family out together would have destroyed published values. A control test pins them.

G5c2 IS NOW IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION, and that was the whole of the remaining corpus
gate. `_rejoin_split_numbered_headings` emits `N. <Heading>`, and its own output was
eligible as its own INPUT: the stacked-orphan guard only saw a BARE `^N.$`, and
`lookup_canonical_label` strips one leading number, so `6. References` still qualified as a
target and a stray `3.` above it was glued on. `3. 6. References` resolves to None, so the
partitioner LOSES the heading. All four remaining non-idempotent papers were this one
shape — efendic_2022_affect, am_sociol_rev_4, nat_comms_3, bmc_med_4 — with DIGIT COUNTS
IDENTICAL across all four, which is why no digit-delta check could ever have found it.

THE RATCHET WAS NOT RAISED. It stays at 0 and the corpus gate now passes on its own terms:
5 non-idempotent papers -> 0, by fixing the causes. The owner was offered a named-defect
list and a raise to 4 and chose to fix the cause before releasing.

`NORMALIZATION_VERSION` 1.9.65 -> 1.9.66. It MUST bump even though this only REMOVES a
rewrite: consumers store extracted text keyed on that string, so leaving it would make text
produced before and after indistinguishable in their store. `TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION`
stays at 2.4.14 — no table code changed.

Two test files, both watched RED first (8 failures on G5c2, 2 on W0g, controls passing) and
both asserting through `normalize_text` / `render_pdf_to_markdown`, never the raw function:
a test that calls a deliberately-kept definition keeps failing after its call sites are
gone, because it measures the definition rather than the product. That trap cost a cycle on
the W0k removal.

Two instrument defects were found and fixed while writing them, both recorded in the files
because both are this repo's own recurring traps: the stacked-heading detector first used
`\s+`, which matches a NEWLINE, so it spanned the three CORRECT lines and reported a defect
on a repaired paper; and it ended in `\S`, which matched a run of bare list numbers. A
render-chain gate that asserted a magic `len(names) >= 50` now asserts that two independent
derivations of the chain AGREE, because a fixed floor can only ever be too low to catch a
blinding or tripped by a deliberate retirement — and it was the second.

Three stale imports of the already-retired W0k/W0l rules are dropped from render.py. They
had sat unused since f169c3d; an unused import of a retired rule reads as though the rule
were still in the pipeline.

Verified: full suite 3209 passed / 0 failed; render_deletion_scan 26/26 papers 0 content
lost; repair_site_scan 120/120; article custody 0 leaks in all three forms; a three-provider
consult round (anthropic/openai/xai, 3 answered 0 refused, all passing the read-the-code
challenge) returned 0 findings. The one adjacent case it raised — a DOTLESS numbering
convention can still stack — was measured at 0 occurrences in 101 papers against a
two-sided control and deliberately left unfixed rather than widened on a constructed string.

recent_commits.message: Make skip_on_api_limit reach zip_peek() and every *_info() listing call via a session option
recent_commits.body:
Follow-up to 7573b210: that commit made skip_on_api_limit reach the
download-level path (download_repo_files() via data_check/code_check/
psychds_check), but two more call sites still had no way to receive it at
all, and both hit a real multi-hour Dryad quota-exhausted 429 wait live
during a full corpus rerun even with skip_on_api_limit = TRUE requested
throughout the reproducibility_check -> data_check chain:

1. repo_check()'s zip_peek() (reads a zip archive's file listing over HTTP
   Range requests, without downloading it) calls the SAME shared retry
   helpers download_repo_files() uses -- .storage_retry_after_factory(),
   .storage_is_transient_factory(), .wait_out_known_rate_limit() -- but has
   no skip_on_api_limit parameter of its own, and repo_check() has no way to
   pass one to it either. These three helpers now fall back to
   getOption("metacheck.skip_on_api_limit", FALSE) whenever their own
   argument is FALSE, so any caller that cannot thread the parameter through
   still gets the right behaviour.

2. Every *_info()/*_links() listing call across archive-*.R (Dryad, Zenodo,
   OSF, Dataverse, Figshare, Mendeley, DataONE, ReShare) shares ONE retry
   function, .batch_query() (R/utils.R), which hardcoded 429 as always
   retryable with no skip option at all -- completely separate from
   download_repo_files()'s retry machinery. It now also checks
   getOption("metacheck.skip_on_api_limit", FALSE) and treats a 429 as
   non-transient when set.

reproducibility_check() sets this option once, for its whole per-paper run
(same temporary-override pattern already used there for llm_use(), restored
unconditionally on exit), so every nested listing call -- however deep, and
regardless of whether that specific function's signature was ever updated
to accept skip_on_api_limit -- respects it without a parameter having to
fan out across ~10 archive backend files individually.

recent_commits.message: Fix definer_lookup crash and thread cache/skip_on_api_limit through reproducibility_check's internal module calls
recent_commits.body:
1. reproducibility_check.R: definer_lookup <- character(0) is read later
   via definer_lookup[[key]] %||% "". `[[` on a named vector throws
   "subscript out of bounds" for a missing key instead of returning NULL,
   crashing on any symbol with 0 or >1 definers. Changed to list().
   Closes #402.

2. code_check.R / data_check.R: neither forwarded its own `cache` argument
   to the module_run(paper, "repo_check", ...) call it makes internally for
   the file listing, so repo_check() fell back to its own default
   (cache = FALSE) regardless of what the caller asked for -- every repo
   listing (Dryad/Zenodo/OSF/...) was re-queried from the host's API from
   scratch on every call. Fixed by forwarding cache = cache at both call
   sites in each file.

3. psychds_check.R / reproducibility_check.R: psychds_check()'s own
   fallback re-fetches data_check's file listing whenever
   get_prev_outputs("data_check", ...) is NULL -- which it always is when
   each module is invoked as a standalone module_run() call rather than a
   chained pipeline, exactly how reproducibility_check() calls it. But
   psychds_check() had no cache/skip_on_api_limit parameters at all, so
   this fallback always ran uncached and un-skip-aware, and
   reproducibility_check()'s own dispatcher excluded psychds_check from
   receiving either (on the assumption that only data_check/code_check
   download files). Net effect, confirmed live: even with
   cache = TRUE, skip_on_api_limit = TRUE requested end-to-end, this one
   fallback call silently ignored both and blocked for hours waiting out
   Dryad's daily quota reset instead of skipping. Fixed by adding both
   parameters to psychds_check() and forwarding them into its fallback
   call, and by including psychds_check in reproducibility_check()'s own
   forwarding list.

   get_prev_outputs("data_check", ...) is NULL -- which it always is when
   each module is invoked as a standalone module_run() call rather than a
   chained pipeline, exactly how reproducibility_check() calls it. But
   psychds_check() had no cache/skip_on_api_limit parameters at all, so
   this fallback always ran uncached and un-skip-aware, and
   reproducibility_check()'s own dispatcher excluded psychds_check from
   receiving either (on the assumption that only data_check/code_check
   download files). Net effect, confirmed live: even with
   cache = TRUE, skip_on_api_limit = TRUE requested end-to-end, this one
   fallback call silently ignored both and blocked for hours waiting out
   Dryad's daily quota reset instead of skipping. Fixed by adding both
   parameters to psychds_check() and forwarding them into its fallback
   call, and by including psychds_check in reproducibility_check()'s own
   forwarding list.

recent_commits.message: Share confirmed rate-limit state across requests to the same host
recent_commits.body:
zip_peek() makes two independent requests per archive (a HEAD then a
Range GET, see .http_range_tail()), and repo_check can call it again
later via download_repo_files()'s .zip_fetch_members() for the same
archive's members. Each of those requests had its own req_retry(), so
when a host was rate-limiting, each one independently discovered a
fresh 429 and paid its own full confirmed-reset wait rather than
reusing what an earlier request already learned.

Confirmed live 2026-09-13 (Cooper validation rerun): one Zenodo record
needing several of these calls produced three consecutive ~40s "Rate
limit reached" waits back to back for what was, from the host's side,
a single rate-limit window.

Adds a session-scoped cache (.host_rate_limit_cache) recording the
last confirmed reset time per host, written by
.storage_retry_after_factory() whenever it learns one, and consulted
via .wait_out_known_rate_limit() immediately before a request is sent
(wired into zip_peek()'s two request helpers and .download_one()) so a
host already known to be rate-limited waits out only the remaining
time once, instead of every subsequent request rediscovering the same
window from scratch.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0g comes out of both text channels — a CI does not tell you which statistic it belongs to
recent_commits.body:
`W0g_dropped_minus_ci_pairing` re-signed a bare positive decimal whenever a bracket in the
same record made the arithmetic work. IT NEVER CHECKED WHICH STATISTIC THE BRACKET
DESCRIBED. On `korbmacher_2022_kruger` the page prints, and pdftotext delivers verbatim:

    r(223) = -0.13 (p = .0498, 95% CI [-0.26, -0.0002])

The interval is `r`'s. W0g took the nearest bare positive decimal in the record — the
P-VALUE — and published `p = -.0498`. A probability cannot be negative. The same paper
yields `p = -.05` from the second occurrence of the shape.

AND IT WAS IN THE SHIPPED OUTPUT, not merely in a re-normalization. The handoff that
scoped this work recorded it as pass-2 only, which reads as an idempotency curiosity. The
render channel called W0g over markdown `normalize_text` had ALREADY normalized, so that
call was itself a second pass: `render_pdf_to_markdown` emitted both fabricated values on
the FIRST render. Raw pdftotext escapes only because it delivers the bracket with EN
DASHES, which W0g's pattern does not match; S5 makes them ASCII and the next pass fires.

THE WIDER COST, confirmed against the rasterized page: over 250 papers W0g fired 12 times
in 4, and at least 7 of those rewrote a quantity that is non-negative by definition —
`SE = 0.11` -> `SE = -0.11`, `p = .90` -> `p = -.90`. `10.1525/collabra.118835` p7 prints
`(hedges' g = -.17, SE = 0.11, 95%CI = [-0.38, 0.04], p = .12)`: a negative estimate with a
POSITIVE standard error, the paper's house style on that page. There was no corruption to
repair.

THE THREE TIERS directive names CI CONTAINMENT verbatim as forbidden evidence, and W0g is
CI containment by name. Its signature is `text: str`, so it can never consult the rendered
page. CHECK THE SIGNATURE BEFORE YOU CHECK THE LOGIC. A "skip the token after `p =`" guard
would fix one paper and not the class: the rule cannot tell which statistic an interval
describes, because that is a fact about the SENTENCE.

BOTH CHANNELS, and only two exist. Verified by grep rather than assumed from this repo's
usual three-channel phrasing: W0g was never wired into `tables/cell_cleaning.py`.

W0b, W0d, W0q, W0h AND W0m ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. A FAMILY VERDICT MUST BE TESTED PER
MEMBER. CLAUDE.md twice records "W0b/W0d/W0g fire 0 times in 226 papers" and that line is
WRONG for the first two — they fire on `efendic_2022_affect` and recover 62 real minus
signs correctly, `r = 2.74 [20.92, 20.30]` back to `r = -.74 [-0.92, -0.30]`. Sweeping the
family out together would have destroyed published values. A control test pins them.

G5c2 IS NOW IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION, and that was the whole of the remaining corpus
gate. `_rejoin_split_numbered_headings` emits `N. <Heading>`, and its own output was
eligible as its own INPUT: the stacked-orphan guard only saw a BARE `^N.$`, and
`lookup_canonical_label` strips one leading number, so `6. References` still qualified as a
target and a stray `3.` above it was glued on. `3. 6. References` resolves to None, so the
partitioner LOSES the heading. All four remaining non-idempotent papers were this one
shape — efendic_2022_affect, am_sociol_rev_4, nat_comms_3, bmc_med_4 — with DIGIT COUNTS
IDENTICAL across all four, which is why no digit-delta check could ever have found it.

THE RATCHET WAS NOT RAISED. It stays at 0 and the corpus gate now passes on its own terms:
5 non-idempotent papers -> 0, by fixing the causes. The owner was offered a named-defect
list and a raise to 4 and chose to fix the cause before releasing.

`NORMALIZATION_VERSION` 1.9.65 -> 1.9.66. It MUST bump even though this only REMOVES a
rewrite: consumers store extracted text keyed on that string, so leaving it would make text
produced before and after indistinguishable in their store. `TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION`
stays at 2.4.14 — no table code changed.

Two test files, both watched RED first (8 failures on G5c2, 2 on W0g, controls passing) and
both asserting through `normalize_text` / `render_pdf_to_markdown`, never the raw function:
a test that calls a deliberately-kept definition keeps failing after its call sites are
gone, because it measures the definition rather than the product. That trap cost a cycle on
the W0k removal.

Two instrument defects were found and fixed while writing them, both recorded in the files
because both are this repo's own recurring traps: the stacked-heading detector first used
`\s+`, which matches a NEWLINE, so it spanned the three CORRECT lines and reported a defect
on a repaired paper; and it ended in `\S`, which matched a run of bare list numbers. A
render-chain gate that asserted a magic `len(names) >= 50` now asserts that two independent
derivations of the chain AGREE, because a fixed floor can only ever be too low to catch a
blinding or tripped by a deliberate retirement — and it was the second.

Three stale imports of the already-retired W0k/W0l rules are dropped from render.py. They
had sat unused since f169c3d; an unused import of a retired rule reads as though the rule
were still in the pipeline.

Verified: full suite 3209 passed / 0 failed; render_deletion_scan 26/26 papers 0 content
lost; repair_site_scan 120/120; article custody 0 leaks in all three forms; a three-provider
consult round (anthropic/openai/xai, 3 answered 0 refused, all passing the read-the-code
challenge) returned 0 findings. The one adjacent case it raised — a DOTLESS numbering
convention can still stack — was measured at 0 occurrences in 101 papers against a
two-sided control and deliberately left unfixed rather than widened on a constructed string.

recent_commits.message: Fix Zenodo crashes on unreadable records and list-column input, add docs
recent_commits.body:
Two real crashes remained after the earlier online()/%empty_or% fix
(c0531ed): (1) a record .zenodo_info() could not read returned only
zenodo_id+error, so a paper whose every Zenodo record was unreadable
produced a table with no doi/license columns at all -- as.character(NULL)
is character(0), and data.frame() rejects mixing that with an n-row
column ("arguments imply differing number of rows"). .zenodo_unread()
now returns the full schema for an unreadable record, and .col_chr()
guards repo_check()'s Zenodo metadata extraction the same way, including
against a list-column element that as.character() silently mangles into
the literal string "character(0)" instead of erroring. (2)
data.frame(zenodo_url = <list>) silently explodes into one column per
list element rather than creating a zenodo_url column, which a list-
column repo_url arriving from repo_check() could trigger; as.character()
before data.frame() fixes it.

added it).

recent_commits.message: Fix reproducibility_check issues #388, #390-392, #394, #396
recent_commits.body:
- #388: classify Bioconductor-only packages (edgeR, DESeq2, phyloseq, ...) as
  source = "bioc" in repro_dependencies() instead of falling through to
  "cran", and install them via BiocManager::install() in repro_install_deps()
  and its Docker equivalent.
- #390: extend the undefined-variable corrective rerun to missing library()
  calls. A "could not find function \"X\"" error with zero same-repo
  definers is checked against a scoped candidate set (the paper's own
  declared dependencies plus a small curated safe-list); an unambiguous
  match is injected as a library() call and the script is rerun once.
- #391: expose per-file modifications (path rewrites, setwd() removal, font
  substitution, library() injections) as a `modifications` data frame in the
  module's output, instead of only aggregate counts.
- #392: fall back to normalised-basename matching for source() targets when
  exact basename matching finds nothing, scoped to code-to-code references
  only (not data files, per the issue's own evidence). Fuzzy matches are
  flagged distinctly via a `fuzzy_sources` attribute, never silently treated
  as exact.
- #394/#396: sniff a .R/.Rmd file's actual content before treating a parse
  failure as a code defect, distinguishing non-R content (JSON/HTML) and
  JAGS/BUGS model definitions from genuine broken R code.

Skipped #389/#393's auto-resolution/guessing scope and #395 (needs a change
in the separate metacheck_docker_reproducibility repo).

recent_commits.message: Fix pre-existing test suite failures unrelated to Zenodo/Mendeley/DataONE work
recent_commits.body:
Found while running the full suite: 15 failures, none in the files this
branch otherwise touches, confirmed against a clean origin/dev checkout.

- data-manifest: the test itself was wrong, not the code -- it left a
  paper's file with no file_location and no failed-download record, which
  .data_check_write_manifest() correctly (per its own documented rules)
  treats as an unreported failure. Fixed the test to actually simulate a
  successful download, which is what it meant to test.
- code_check manifest: a real cross-contamination bug -- jsonlite::toJSON()
  renders an R NULL list element as "{}" rather than dropping it, so an
  absent packages/files_failed section for one paper in a batch came back
  as a non-NULL empty object instead of NULL when read back. Filtered NULLs
  before writing, matching the convention .data_check_write_manifest()
  already uses. Also added the code_install_packages column (#398) to two
  tests never updated for it.
- repo-download: the real cause of 9 failures -- testthat::local_mocked_
  bindings() for httr2::req_perform/req_perform_parallel silently fails to
  restore the original binding in this testthat 3.3.2 / withr 3.0.3 /
  httr2 1.3.0 combination (confirmed with a canary: deferred cleanup fires
  in general, this specific namespace restore just doesn't stick), so a
  mock from one test broke every real download in every later test in the
  file. Added an explicit, unconditional top-level restore after each risky
  mock. One remaining failure was a tight 3s wall-clock threshold that's
  simply slow on this machine; loosened it since the regression it guards
  against (an O(n) scan over 20000 rows) would take far longer regardless.

recent_commits.message: Add Mendeley Data and DataONE repository support
recent_commits.body:
Mendeley Data: detects 10.17632/ DOIs and data.mendeley.com URLs, queried
via the public, unauthenticated data.mendeley.com/public-api/datasets/<id>
endpoint. Host-independent by design -- verified live that an institution's
white-labelled front end (e.g. Washington University's "Digital Commons
Data") serves the exact same backend, so detection only needs the DOI, not
a host registry.

DataONE: a federation of independently-run repositories ("member nodes"),
not one hosted service. Covers four verified hosts (Arctic Data Center,
KNB, Taiwan Forestry Research Institute, Smithsonian Tropical Data Portal
-- the latter two found via re3data.org), each confirmed live and each
mounting the same underlying REST API at a different base path per
installation. Parses each dataset's EML metadata document for its file
listing.

Both wired into repo_check.R the same way as the existing providers, and
tested end-to-end against real live records through the full repo_check()
pipeline.

recent_commits.message: Fix Zenodo online() DNS false-negatives and harden %||% against zero-length JSON fields
recent_commits.body:
online() previously failed a paper's entire Zenodo retrieval on a single
transient DNS lookup miss; it now retries. Zenodo also silently dropped
records when a JSON field came back as a length-zero value (e.g. an empty
array) rather than NULL, since %||% only guards against NULL -- this threw
"arguments imply differing number of rows" inside a tryCatch that quietly
discarded the whole record. Confirmed against real corpus failures.

Added %empty_or% (like %||%, but also catches length-zero values) and
applied it everywhere the same bare-%||% gap existed: Dataverse, Dryad,
DSpace7, Figshare, GitHub, GitLab, OSF, PsychArchives, and ReShare.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0g comes out of both text channels — a CI does not tell you which statistic it belongs to
recent_commits.body:
`W0g_dropped_minus_ci_pairing` re-signed a bare positive decimal whenever a bracket in the
same record made the arithmetic work. IT NEVER CHECKED WHICH STATISTIC THE BRACKET
DESCRIBED. On `korbmacher_2022_kruger` the page prints, and pdftotext delivers verbatim:

    r(223) = -0.13 (p = .0498, 95% CI [-0.26, -0.0002])

The interval is `r`'s. W0g took the nearest bare positive decimal in the record — the
P-VALUE — and published `p = -.0498`. A probability cannot be negative. The same paper
yields `p = -.05` from the second occurrence of the shape.

AND IT WAS IN THE SHIPPED OUTPUT, not merely in a re-normalization. The handoff that
scoped this work recorded it as pass-2 only, which reads as an idempotency curiosity. The
render channel called W0g over markdown `normalize_text` had ALREADY normalized, so that
call was itself a second pass: `render_pdf_to_markdown` emitted both fabricated values on
the FIRST render. Raw pdftotext escapes only because it delivers the bracket with EN
DASHES, which W0g's pattern does not match; S5 makes them ASCII and the next pass fires.

THE WIDER COST, confirmed against the rasterized page: over 250 papers W0g fired 12 times
in 4, and at least 7 of those rewrote a quantity that is non-negative by definition —
`SE = 0.11` -> `SE = -0.11`, `p = .90` -> `p = -.90`. `10.1525/collabra.118835` p7 prints
`(hedges' g = -.17, SE = 0.11, 95%CI = [-0.38, 0.04], p = .12)`: a negative estimate with a
POSITIVE standard error, the paper's house style on that page. There was no corruption to
repair.

THE THREE TIERS directive names CI CONTAINMENT verbatim as forbidden evidence, and W0g is
CI containment by name. Its signature is `text: str`, so it can never consult the rendered
page. CHECK THE SIGNATURE BEFORE YOU CHECK THE LOGIC. A "skip the token after `p =`" guard
would fix one paper and not the class: the rule cannot tell which statistic an interval
describes, because that is a fact about the SENTENCE.

BOTH CHANNELS, and only two exist. Verified by grep rather than assumed from this repo's
usual three-channel phrasing: W0g was never wired into `tables/cell_cleaning.py`.

W0b, W0d, W0q, W0h AND W0m ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. A FAMILY VERDICT MUST BE TESTED PER
MEMBER. CLAUDE.md twice records "W0b/W0d/W0g fire 0 times in 226 papers" and that line is
WRONG for the first two — they fire on `efendic_2022_affect` and recover 62 real minus
signs correctly, `r = 2.74 [20.92, 20.30]` back to `r = -.74 [-0.92, -0.30]`. Sweeping the
family out together would have destroyed published values. A control test pins them.

G5c2 IS NOW IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION, and that was the whole of the remaining corpus
gate. `_rejoin_split_numbered_headings` emits `N. <Heading>`, and its own output was
eligible as its own INPUT: the stacked-orphan guard only saw a BARE `^N.$`, and
`lookup_canonical_label` strips one leading number, so `6. References` still qualified as a
target and a stray `3.` above it was glued on. `3. 6. References` resolves to None, so the
partitioner LOSES the heading. All four remaining non-idempotent papers were this one
shape — efendic_2022_affect, am_sociol_rev_4, nat_comms_3, bmc_med_4 — with DIGIT COUNTS
IDENTICAL across all four, which is why no digit-delta check could ever have found it.

THE RATCHET WAS NOT RAISED. It stays at 0 and the corpus gate now passes on its own terms:
5 non-idempotent papers -> 0, by fixing the causes. The owner was offered a named-defect
list and a raise to 4 and chose to fix the cause before releasing.

`NORMALIZATION_VERSION` 1.9.65 -> 1.9.66. It MUST bump even though this only REMOVES a
rewrite: consumers store extracted text keyed on that string, so leaving it would make text
produced before and after indistinguishable in their store. `TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION`
stays at 2.4.14 — no table code changed.

Two test files, both watched RED first (8 failures on G5c2, 2 on W0g, controls passing) and
both asserting through `normalize_text` / `render_pdf_to_markdown`, never the raw function:
a test that calls a deliberately-kept definition keeps failing after its call sites are
gone, because it measures the definition rather than the product. That trap cost a cycle on
the W0k removal.

Two instrument defects were found and fixed while writing them, both recorded in the files
because both are this repo's own recurring traps: the stacked-heading detector first used
`\s+`, which matches a NEWLINE, so it spanned the three CORRECT lines and reported a defect
on a repaired paper; and it ended in `\S`, which matched a run of bare list numbers. A
render-chain gate that asserted a magic `len(names) >= 50` now asserts that two independent
derivations of the chain AGREE, because a fixed floor can only ever be too low to catch a
blinding or tripped by a deliberate retirement — and it was the second.

Three stale imports of the already-retired W0k/W0l rules are dropped from render.py. They
had sat unused since f169c3d; an unused import of a retired rule reads as though the rule
were still in the pipeline.

Verified: full suite 3209 passed / 0 failed; render_deletion_scan 26/26 papers 0 content
lost; repair_site_scan 120/120; article custody 0 leaks in all three forms; a three-provider
consult round (anthropic/openai/xai, 3 answered 0 refused, all passing the read-the-code
challenge) returned 0 findings. The one adjacent case it raised — a DOTLESS numbering
convention can still stack — was measured at 0 occurrences in 101 papers against a
two-sided control and deliberately left unfixed rather than widened on a constructed string.

repo_url and drop those files from the file listing entirely, before
classification, so they never inflate files_n/files_code or appear in
downstream reports.

Research Collection) found and verified the same way.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0g comes out of both text channels — a CI does not tell you which statistic it belongs to
recent_commits.body:
`W0g_dropped_minus_ci_pairing` re-signed a bare positive decimal whenever a bracket in the
same record made the arithmetic work. IT NEVER CHECKED WHICH STATISTIC THE BRACKET
DESCRIBED. On `korbmacher_2022_kruger` the page prints, and pdftotext delivers verbatim:

    r(223) = -0.13 (p = .0498, 95% CI [-0.26, -0.0002])

The interval is `r`'s. W0g took the nearest bare positive decimal in the record — the
P-VALUE — and published `p = -.0498`. A probability cannot be negative. The same paper
yields `p = -.05` from the second occurrence of the shape.

AND IT WAS IN THE SHIPPED OUTPUT, not merely in a re-normalization. The handoff that
scoped this work recorded it as pass-2 only, which reads as an idempotency curiosity. The
render channel called W0g over markdown `normalize_text` had ALREADY normalized, so that
call was itself a second pass: `render_pdf_to_markdown` emitted both fabricated values on
the FIRST render. Raw pdftotext escapes only because it delivers the bracket with EN
DASHES, which W0g's pattern does not match; S5 makes them ASCII and the next pass fires.

THE WIDER COST, confirmed against the rasterized page: over 250 papers W0g fired 12 times
in 4, and at least 7 of those rewrote a quantity that is non-negative by definition —
`SE = 0.11` -> `SE = -0.11`, `p = .90` -> `p = -.90`. `10.1525/collabra.118835` p7 prints
`(hedges' g = -.17, SE = 0.11, 95%CI = [-0.38, 0.04], p = .12)`: a negative estimate with a
POSITIVE standard error, the paper's house style on that page. There was no corruption to
repair.

THE THREE TIERS directive names CI CONTAINMENT verbatim as forbidden evidence, and W0g is
CI containment by name. Its signature is `text: str`, so it can never consult the rendered
page. CHECK THE SIGNATURE BEFORE YOU CHECK THE LOGIC. A "skip the token after `p =`" guard
would fix one paper and not the class: the rule cannot tell which statistic an interval
describes, because that is a fact about the SENTENCE.

BOTH CHANNELS, and only two exist. Verified by grep rather than assumed from this repo's
usual three-channel phrasing: W0g was never wired into `tables/cell_cleaning.py`.

W0b, W0d, W0q, W0h AND W0m ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. A FAMILY VERDICT MUST BE TESTED PER
MEMBER. CLAUDE.md twice records "W0b/W0d/W0g fire 0 times in 226 papers" and that line is
WRONG for the first two — they fire on `efendic_2022_affect` and recover 62 real minus
signs correctly, `r = 2.74 [20.92, 20.30]` back to `r = -.74 [-0.92, -0.30]`. Sweeping the
family out together would have destroyed published values. A control test pins them.

G5c2 IS NOW IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION, and that was the whole of the remaining corpus
gate. `_rejoin_split_numbered_headings` emits `N. <Heading>`, and its own output was
eligible as its own INPUT: the stacked-orphan guard only saw a BARE `^N.$`, and
`lookup_canonical_label` strips one leading number, so `6. References` still qualified as a
target and a stray `3.` above it was glued on. `3. 6. References` resolves to None, so the
partitioner LOSES the heading. All four remaining non-idempotent papers were this one
shape — efendic_2022_affect, am_sociol_rev_4, nat_comms_3, bmc_med_4 — with DIGIT COUNTS
IDENTICAL across all four, which is why no digit-delta check could ever have found it.

THE RATCHET WAS NOT RAISED. It stays at 0 and the corpus gate now passes on its own terms:
5 non-idempotent papers -> 0, by fixing the causes. The owner was offered a named-defect
list and a raise to 4 and chose to fix the cause before releasing.

`NORMALIZATION_VERSION` 1.9.65 -> 1.9.66. It MUST bump even though this only REMOVES a
rewrite: consumers store extracted text keyed on that string, so leaving it would make text
produced before and after indistinguishable in their store. `TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION`
stays at 2.4.14 — no table code changed.

Two test files, both watched RED first (8 failures on G5c2, 2 on W0g, controls passing) and
both asserting through `normalize_text` / `render_pdf_to_markdown`, never the raw function:
a test that calls a deliberately-kept definition keeps failing after its call sites are
gone, because it measures the definition rather than the product. That trap cost a cycle on
the W0k removal.

Two instrument defects were found and fixed while writing them, both recorded in the files
because both are this repo's own recurring traps: the stacked-heading detector first used
`\s+`, which matches a NEWLINE, so it spanned the three CORRECT lines and reported a defect
on a repaired paper; and it ended in `\S`, which matched a run of bare list numbers. A
render-chain gate that asserted a magic `len(names) >= 50` now asserts that two independent
derivations of the chain AGREE, because a fixed floor can only ever be too low to catch a
blinding or tripped by a deliberate retirement — and it was the second.

Three stale imports of the already-retired W0k/W0l rules are dropped from render.py. They
had sat unused since f169c3d; an unused import of a retired rule reads as though the rule
were still in the pipeline.

Verified: full suite 3209 passed / 0 failed; render_deletion_scan 26/26 papers 0 content
lost; repair_site_scan 120/120; article custody 0 leaks in all three forms; a three-provider
consult round (anthropic/openai/xai, 3 answered 0 refused, all passing the read-the-code
challenge) returned 0 findings. The one adjacent case it raised — a DOTLESS numbering
convention can still stack — was measured at 0 occurrences in 101 papers against a
two-sided control and deliberately left unfixed rather than widened on a constructed string.

recent_commits.message: docs(changelog): drop the absolute offsets — they do not transfer; keep the gap, which does
recent_commits.body:
843394a published `char 60080 intact / char 60155 destroyed` from a consumer's pre-fix store.
The labels were right, but the numbers should not have been published at all, and measuring it
here is what showed why:

    consumer's 1.9.57 store   HapMap3 @ 60080   HapMap * @ 60155
    my 1.9.65 re-extraction   HapMap3 @ 60110   HapMap3   @ 60185

SAME PAPER, SAME TWO OCCURRENCES, DIFFERENT ABSOLUTE POSITIONS. An offset is a property of one
extraction's exact text, not of the defect, so a consumer running `grep -ob` against its own
store would meet a discrepancy with an entirely mundane cause -- while already anxious about
corrupted data. Byte and character offsets differ AGAIN within a single file (43 bytes of
multi-byte UTF-8 upstream in that store, so `grep -ob` reports 60096 where python reports
60080), which would force the unit to be stated as well.

WHAT TRANSFERS IS THE GAP, and it is the load-bearing half: the two occurrences are 75 apart,
IDENTICAL IN CHARACTERS AND IN BYTES, measured independently by both parties on two different
extractions. The text between them is a single sentence boundary:

    HapMap3 SNPs. Inclusion in the LD Score regression analysis was limited to

So "same token, same paragraph, 75 apart, one rewritten and one not" survives every way of
measuring it, and that is the sentence a consumer needs. The counts (`HapMap3` = 1,
`HapMap *` = 1 pre-fix) are the other durable part. The offsets were the most fragile thing in
the block and the only part nobody could reproduce.

The general point, worth more than this edit: A NUMBER THAT CANNOT BE REPRODUCED BY THE AUDIENCE
IS NOT EVIDENCE TO THEM, IT IS AN INVITATION TO A CONTRADICTION. Publish the invariant, not the
coordinate.

Raised by the consumer that supplied the original figures, who also corrected their own prose
(they had described character offsets as byte offsets). Verified here rather than relayed.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: docs(changelog): the pre-fix half — 2 in the source, 1 destroyed, 75 characters apart
recent_commits.body:
5036c9a reproduced the POST-fix side from the custody PDF (HapMap3 = 2 at normalization 1.9.65)
and that settled whether the original claim held. It could not show what an AFFECTED file looks
like, because docpluck no longer produces one. The consumer supplied that half from its own
1.9.57 store, with byte offsets and a control this time:

    corpus-text__docpluck-norm@1.9.57.txt  (112,876 B)
      char 60080  INTACT     "...focusing on HapMap3 SNPs. Inclusion in the LD Score regression..."
      char 60155  DESTROYED  "...limited to HapMap * SNPs with a minor allele frequency (MAF)..."
      HapMap3 = 1     HapMap * = 1     HapMap 3 = 0

Put beside the post-fix measurement the whole picture is there: 2 occurrences in the source, 1
destroyed before the fix, 0 after.

THE TWO SURVIVORS ARE 75 CHARACTERS APART, IN CONSECUTIVE SENTENCES. That is the sharpest
statement of why a single site settles nothing: the same token, the same paragraph, one rewritten
and one not. A scan that stops at the first hit reads whichever it happens to meet, and either
answer is defensible from the evidence it looked at.

ONE PRACTICAL SOFTENING, and it is the consumer's correction to my wording rather than mine: an
intact sibling may sit nearby, so a consumer can SOMETIMES recover the original by scanning.
Re-extraction at 1.9.65+ is the RELIABLE route, not the ONLY one. An intermediate revision of the
notice said "only", which overstates the damage and would send someone re-running a pipeline when
a grep would have answered it.

For the record on the exchange that produced this: their retraction and my re-correction crossed
in flight, so their "STOP, revert 0febe36" arrived after 5036c9a had already reverted it. Both
sides converged on the same reproduced answer independently, which is the useful property of
having measured it rather than argued it.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: docs(changelog): withdraw yesterday's correction — I published a consumer's claim without reproducing it
recent_commits.body:
The paragraph added in 0febe36 said "both forms coexist" is not a general property of the W0k
damage, on a consumer's report that its copy of 10.1038/s41562-024-02076-3 held only the
destroyed form. Its author has withdrawn it. **The error on this side is that I edited a PUBLIC
document on a relayed measurement I had not reproduced** -- and this project's own rule is that a
reviewer's finding is a HYPOTHESIS until a local reproduction confirms it. Two hops, no
verification, and it reached the public CHANGELOG and the notice every consumer is acting on.

REPRODUCED NOW, at the source, which is what should have happened first:

    10.1038/s41562-024-02076-3, re-extracted from the custody PDF at normalization 1.9.65
      HapMap3  = 2       HapMap 3 = 0       HapMap * = 0
        "...focusing on HapMap3 SNPs. Inclusion in the LD Score regression..."
        "...analysis was limited to HapMap3 SNPs with a minor allele frequency..."

    10.1073/pnas.2313604121, same method
      Deposited 3 = 1    Deposited * = 0
        "Deposited 3 December 2022."

Both occurrences of the identifier are `HapMap3` in the source, and the pre-fix pipeline
destroyed exactly ONE of the two. So the ORIGINAL claim was right and is now measured rather than
relayed, and the date shape is independently confirmed rather than taken on trust.

THE RULE RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and only one half was written down before: a single clean site
cannot clear a document, AND a single destroyed site does not condemn one. Count every
occurrence.

HOW THE WRONG CLAIM WAS MANUFACTURED, because the mechanism is more useful than the correction.
The consumer verified with `grep -c 'HapMap 3'` -- WITH A SPACE -- against an intact form that
has none. They searched for a string that cannot exist, got 0, and read that zero as a finding.
`HapMap 3` returns 0 against a fully intact file; the trap is now demonstrated rather than
predicted, and it fired in the SAME message that flagged the no-space trap to others.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE LESSON. Their 30-file statistics scan carried two-sided controls and held up
completely. The claim that failed was a one-line verification grep, where nobody thinks to plant
a control. Knowing a failure mode by name does not prevent it; a control does, and effort tracks
the ceremony of the check rather than the weight of the conclusion drawn from it.

Nothing else in 0febe36 is affected: the date shape stands (verified above), and the measured
"no published statistic corrupted across 30 files" result stands with its controls intact.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: docs(changelog): "both forms coexist" is NOT general, and W0k also destroyed a bare DATE digit
recent_commits.body:
Two corrections to the 2.4.140 section, both from a consumer's own measurement rather than from
this repo, and both making the picture WORSE in one direction and better in another.

1. THE RECOVERY CLAIM WAS TOO OPTIMISTIC. This file said `10.1038/s41562-024-02076-3` holds both
   `HapMap3 SNPs.` intact and `HapMap *` destroyed, and drew "a single clean site cannot clear a
   document". True of the copy examined here. But in the CONSUMER'S copy at normalization 1.9.57
   the token is destroyed at EVERY occurrence -- `HapMap3` count 0, `HapMap 3` count 0 -- so
   there is nothing in that file to recover from. "Both forms coexist" is a property of one
   extraction, not of the defect. Re-extraction from the source PDF is then the only route, which
   is a materially different instruction to give a consumer.

2. A THIRD SHAPE, WITH A REAL DOI. `10.1073/pnas.2313604121` shipped `Deposited * December 2022.`
   for `Deposited 3 December 2022.` -- a bare day-of-month digit with SPACES ON BOTH SIDES. Every
   example previously recorded (HapMap3, ASL TO3, GRCh3, Material 3, x3) was a digit glued to a
   word or an identifier, so a pattern anchored to that shape misses this class entirely. Verified
   by re-extracting the custody PDF through a service at identity 2.4.141/3f035f5/clean, not by
   pattern-matching. This meets the project's standing rule that a case comes from a real paper
   with the DOI recorded, never from a constructed string.

   Two grep traps follow and are now written down: the intact form is `HapMap3` with NO space, so
   grepping `HapMap 3` returns 0 and reads as a failed fix; and the standalone-digit class needs
   its own pattern.

3. THE REASSURING HALF, AND IT IS MEASURED. Across that consumer's 30-file corpus NO PUBLISHED
   STATISTIC was corrupted. The unambiguous signature is a star sandwiched between digits -- a
   significance star can never sit there -- and it returned 0 sites in 30 files under a TWO-SIDED
   control: planted `12*4` and `0.6*9` caught, planted `0.695***` and `0.34**` ignored, 1,094
   asterisks counted to prove the files were read, and 0 surviving `×`/`✕`/`⨯` glyphs to prove the
   asterisk surface was complete rather than a subset. The damage class is identifiers, names and
   dates -- not statistics.

THEIR PROCESS IS WORTH RECORDING AS MUCH AS THEIR RESULT. Their first scan flagged
`240 participants * 8 items` as corruption and the NEGATIVE control caught it. A later pass
reported "0 corrupted statistics" while its own POSITIVE control was dead -- the planted string
contained no genuine digit-star-digit, so the pattern had never been exercised and that zero was
untested rather than clean. Both are exactly the "a zero is a claim about the instrument" failure
this project keeps re-learning, caught here by controls rather than by luck.

The same consumer independently reproduced this release's "PDF table output is byte-identical"
claim: `flattened_row_count`, `flattened_row_field_keys` and `flattened_row_keys` unchanged
across table extraction 2.4.12 -> 2.4.14 on their PDF fixture.

The consumer notice carries all of the above.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.body:
`docs/NORMALIZATION.md` and `docs/SCOPE.md` are the files this project points consumers at --
SYMBOL_CONTRACT.md opens with "if you maintain a tool that parses docpluck's output, this page
is your interface" -- and both still listed W0i/W0k/W0l as live and classified them

recent_commits.message: fix(pin): the bump commit carries the frontend mirror, or it does not happen
recent_commits.body:
`check_app_pin_sync.py --fix` rewrote service/requirements.txt and then staged
that ONE path. frontend/docpluck-pin.json is a committed mirror of the same pin
and was never regenerated or added, so every --fix run pushed a master whose own
suite was red on frontend/src/lib/errors/docpluck-pin.test.ts.

WHY THE MIRROR EXISTS: the documented CLI deploy is `cd frontend && vercel --prod`,
which uploads ONLY frontend/ and therefore cannot read ../service/requirements.txt.
Without a fresh mirror that build falls back to the hand-maintained DOCPLUCK_VERSION
env var -- the 50-day-stale cache-key failure the derivation was built to remove.

IT HAD ALREADY HAPPENED. 54c9a31 bumped the pin to v2.4.138 and stranded the mirror
at 2.4.137. Nobody noticed until a QA session went looking an hour before this
release -- because the failure is SILENT in this repo and lands as red tests in the
app's suite, which this project does not run. Reported by the pdfextractor-65 and
docpluck-ef sessions; VERIFIED HERE AT THE SOURCE before acting on it (line 221 was
the function's only `git add`, and a two-sided grep found 8 hits for "requirements"
against 0 for pin.json/frontend/mirror/sync-pin, so the instrument worked).

THE FIX CALLS THE EXISTING GENERATOR rather than writing the JSON in Python: one
concept, one implementation. A second copy of the mirror format here would drift
from frontend/scripts/sync-docpluck-pin.mjs silently, which is the failure this
project's "ONE CONCEPT, ONE TABLE" rule exists to prevent. A missing `node` is a
HARD FAILURE, never a skip -- skipping is the original defect wearing a green tick,
and the resulting commit would push a red master.

TESTS, watched RED FIRST against the unpatched function and re-verified red after
the third assertion was corrected: 3 failed / 0 passed unpatched, 3 passed patched.
The fixture copies the REAL generator instead of reimplementing it, and the
"both paths staged" test asserts requirements.txt is present FIRST, as a control so
the mirror assertion cannot pass vacuously.

ONE THING WENT WRONG WRITING THEM, recorded because it is this repo's own recurring
trap: the missing-generator test first asked whether the mirror path appeared in
HEAD's file list -- true of the FIXTURE'S base commit, so it failed against correct
code and would have been "fixed" by weakening it. It now compares the HEAD sha,
which is the question that was meant: did this call create a commit at all?

AND THE HARDCODED SIBLING NAME IS GONE. Locating the consumer checkout is now
STRUCTURAL -- the sibling whose service/requirements.txt carries a docpluck pin --
with $DOCPLUCK_APP_REPO and --app-repo as overrides. Two reasons, and the second is
the durable one: this repo is PUBLIC and a hardcoded name published the private
consumer's layout (the public-repo guard blocked the commit that merely MOVED the
literal, which is the gate working); and a name is the more fragile key anyway,
since relocating the checkout would have sent this gate at a path that does not
exist. It returns None rather than a plausible-but-wrong path, so "found nothing"
cannot be misread as "checkout has moved".

Six tests. The resolver's own three are two-sided: a decoy sibling with the right
SHAPE but no pin, sorted FIRST so a resolver that took the first match would fail;
a layout where nothing matches, asserting None rather than a guess; and the env
override. Verified at the REAL call site too -- running the gate resolves the
checkout and reads the pin from origin/master, which a wrong directory could not
do. That run also caught a NameError the refactor introduced (`lib_repo` was still
used further down), which no unit test would have reached.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(hygiene): two internal-process words in a PUBLIC repo's source comments
recent_commits.body:
`giladfeldman/docpluck` is public (`gh repo view --json isPrivate` -> false), and the
public-repo guard flagged two words on the two version-constant lines this release touched:
"ESCIcheck handoff 2026-06-25" and "found by a conductor fleet sweep". A handoff and the
conductor seat are internal coordination, not part of the published contract. Rewritten as
"ESCIcheck consumer request" and "a portfolio-wide sweep" -- neither loses a fact.

The consumer NAMES on the same lines (effectcheck / escimate / scimeto) are deliberately kept:
they are already public in docs/SCOPE.md, docs/SYMBOL_CONTRACT.md and docs/README.md, where

recent_commits.message: docs(changelog): drop the absolute offsets — they do not transfer; keep the gap, which does
recent_commits.body:
843394a published `char 60080 intact / char 60155 destroyed` from a consumer's pre-fix store.
The labels were right, but the numbers should not have been published at all, and measuring it
here is what showed why:

    consumer's 1.9.57 store   HapMap3 @ 60080   HapMap * @ 60155
    my 1.9.65 re-extraction   HapMap3 @ 60110   HapMap3   @ 60185

SAME PAPER, SAME TWO OCCURRENCES, DIFFERENT ABSOLUTE POSITIONS. An offset is a property of one
extraction's exact text, not of the defect, so a consumer running `grep -ob` against its own
store would meet a discrepancy with an entirely mundane cause -- while already anxious about
corrupted data. Byte and character offsets differ AGAIN within a single file (43 bytes of
multi-byte UTF-8 upstream in that store, so `grep -ob` reports 60096 where python reports
60080), which would force the unit to be stated as well.

WHAT TRANSFERS IS THE GAP, and it is the load-bearing half: the two occurrences are 75 apart,
IDENTICAL IN CHARACTERS AND IN BYTES, measured independently by both parties on two different
extractions. The text between them is a single sentence boundary:

    HapMap3 SNPs. Inclusion in the LD Score regression analysis was limited to

So "same token, same paragraph, 75 apart, one rewritten and one not" survives every way of
measuring it, and that is the sentence a consumer needs. The counts (`HapMap3` = 1,
`HapMap *` = 1 pre-fix) are the other durable part. The offsets were the most fragile thing in
the block and the only part nobody could reproduce.

The general point, worth more than this edit: A NUMBER THAT CANNOT BE REPRODUCED BY THE AUDIENCE
IS NOT EVIDENCE TO THEM, IT IS AN INVITATION TO A CONTRADICTION. Publish the invariant, not the
coordinate.

Raised by the consumer that supplied the original figures, who also corrected their own prose
(they had described character offsets as byte offsets). Verified here rather than relayed.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: docs(changelog): the pre-fix half — 2 in the source, 1 destroyed, 75 characters apart
recent_commits.body:
5036c9a reproduced the POST-fix side from the custody PDF (HapMap3 = 2 at normalization 1.9.65)
and that settled whether the original claim held. It could not show what an AFFECTED file looks
like, because docpluck no longer produces one. The consumer supplied that half from its own
1.9.57 store, with byte offsets and a control this time:

    corpus-text__docpluck-norm@1.9.57.txt  (112,876 B)
      char 60080  INTACT     "...focusing on HapMap3 SNPs. Inclusion in the LD Score regression..."
      char 60155  DESTROYED  "...limited to HapMap * SNPs with a minor allele frequency (MAF)..."
      HapMap3 = 1     HapMap * = 1     HapMap 3 = 0

Put beside the post-fix measurement the whole picture is there: 2 occurrences in the source, 1
destroyed before the fix, 0 after.

THE TWO SURVIVORS ARE 75 CHARACTERS APART, IN CONSECUTIVE SENTENCES. That is the sharpest
statement of why a single site settles nothing: the same token, the same paragraph, one rewritten
and one not. A scan that stops at the first hit reads whichever it happens to meet, and either
answer is defensible from the evidence it looked at.

ONE PRACTICAL SOFTENING, and it is the consumer's correction to my wording rather than mine: an
intact sibling may sit nearby, so a consumer can SOMETIMES recover the original by scanning.
Re-extraction at 1.9.65+ is the RELIABLE route, not the ONLY one. An intermediate revision of the
notice said "only", which overstates the damage and would send someone re-running a pipeline when
a grep would have answered it.

For the record on the exchange that produced this: their retraction and my re-correction crossed
in flight, so their "STOP, revert 0febe36" arrived after 5036c9a had already reverted it. Both
sides converged on the same reproduced answer independently, which is the useful property of
having measured it rather than argued it.
